title: Aggrega Wasm Search Socket
description: The JSON wire shapes the search.wasm plugin socket consumes and emits. A search plugin answers a ranked full-text query over an indexed content set: the host hands the guest a query on its search export (SearchInput) and the guest returns the ranked results it found (SearchOutput). The guest owns the index and the ranking; the host routes the query and carries the results without interpreting them, so ordering is the guest's responsibility — identical input must produce identical results in identical order. The wire shapes are generated into each ABI language from this schema, and per-language round-trip tests assert the three codecs produce one byte-identical wire.

SearchInput.description: The payload the host hands a search plugin on its search export: the query string, an optional cap on how many results to return, and an optional set of field filters that narrow the search. The guest interprets the query and the filters against its own index; the host does not parse them.

query.description: The full-text query the guest answers. The guest owns the query grammar; the host carries the string verbatim and does not parse it.

limit.description: The maximum number of ranked results the guest returns. Zero or absent asks the guest for its own default result count; a positive value caps the result set at that size.

filters.description: An optional set of field filters that narrow the search, keyed by field name to the value the guest matches against. Keys serialize in sorted order so the payload is byte-identical across runs of identical input. Absent or empty applies no filter. The guest owns the filter field vocabulary; the host carries the pairs verbatim and does not interpret them.

SearchResult.description: One ranked result the guest returns: the document it matched, a human-readable title, an in-document anchor, a short snippet of matching context, and the relevance score the guest assigned. The host carries every field verbatim and interprets none of them.

doc_id.description: The identity of the matched document within the guest's index, an opaque identifier the host carries verbatim (for example a document path or a stable content id).

title.description: The human-readable title of the matched document, for display in the result list.

anchor.description: The in-document anchor the match points at, so a consumer can navigate to the matching section rather than the document head. Empty when the match is document-level and carries no finer anchor.

snippet.description: A short excerpt of the matching context, for display alongside the title. Empty when the guest returns no excerpt.

score.description: The relevance score the guest assigned this result. Higher is more relevant; the scale is the guest's own. The host orders nothing by it — the guest returns results already ranked — but carries it so a consumer can display or threshold on relevance.

SearchOutput.description: The payload a search plugin returns from its search export: the ranked results it found, in descending relevance order. The guest owns the ranking; the host carries the list verbatim and preserves its order. An empty results list means the query matched nothing.

results.description: The ranked results the guest found, in the descending relevance order the guest assigned. The host preserves the order so the payload is byte-identical across runs of identical input.
